name: concat-build
axis: string building by repeated single-character append (the quadratic trap)
notes: REPS independent N-character strings, built one character at a time (n = total appends). Doubling N (not REPS) is the asymptote diagnostic; measured: VL x3.48 = O(n^2), every `+` allocates a fresh WasmGC i32 array and copies both operands. Rust x1.63, deno x1.88, Python x1.77 — all O(n) once the fixed startup/JIT cost is removed. `s += c` compiles to exactly the same thing as `s = s + c` in VL (2101 vs 2126 ms), so there is no faster spelling of the idiom. Python runs REPS=250, a 4x reduction. opt.vl routes through the `fromCodePoints(i32[])` builtin and is a DEFECT witness, not a recommendation.
void: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT: cross-language ratio is unusable. The Rust column measures NOTHING — min-of-7 pinned wall time is 4.6ms, BELOW the 6.8ms empty-Rust-program startup baseline. deno reads 56.0ms (34% launcher) and python3 71.5ms (17% launcher); VL reads 1730ms. No REPS value fixes this: work is linear in REPS for Rust/JS/Py but VL is O(n^2) in N and linear in REPS, so REPS x20 puts Rust at ~92ms (still under the 200ms floor) and VL at ~34s. The VL-INTERNAL finding survives and should still be reported: doubling N multiplies VL by ~3.5x (O(n^2)) while Rust/JS/Python stay ~1.6-1.9x (O(n)) — VL's `s = s + c` reallocates and copies both operands every append. Do not publish any Rust/JS/Python-vs-VL multiple from this directory.

audit.startupBaseline: measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
